mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on Team B matches where both recent shots (RECENT_5) fall below their ALL_PRIOR baseline AND recent shots_on_target (RECENT_5) fall below their ALL_PRIOR baseline simultaneously. Measure whether goals FOR in those matches are suppressed relative to matches where only one or neither observable is below baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Goals FOR rises with shots volume and shots-on-target ratio jointly; when both are simultaneously below baseline the suppression of goals FOR is greater than the sum of each individual suppression
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shot volume has declined sharply in recent matches while the shots-on-target conversion rate (shots on target as a share of total shots) has also deteriorated, suggesting a joint degradation in both attacking volume and quality that is not captured by either observable alone. When a team's recent shots are simultaneously low and their on-target ratio is low relative to their own long-run baseline, their goal output is suppressed beyond what either observable individually predicts.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint two-observable conditioning (shots AND shots_on_target both below baseline simultaneously) rather than a single observable against one band. Neither a shots mirror nor a shots_on_target mirror alone captures the interaction between volume and accuracy.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on match contexts where Team B's shots AGAINST (RECENT_5) exceeds their ALL_PRIOR baseline AND Team A's shots FOR (RECENT_5) exceeds Team A's ALL_PRIOR baseline simultaneously. Measure whether total shots and shots_on_target in those matches are elevated relative to matches where only one side's trend is elevated.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total match shots and shots_on_target rise when both the attacking team's recent shot production and the defending team's recent shot-allowance are simultaneously above their respective long-run baselines, with the joint condition producing greater elevation than either condition alone
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B concedes substantially more shots and shots-on-target in recent matches than their long-run average, while Team A's recent shots and shots-on-target FOR have also risen above their long-run average. The joint condition of one team's defensive shot-allowance rising while the opponent's attacking shot production is also rising creates a compounding exposure that is structurally different from either team's individual defensive or offensive observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires conditioning on two distinct opponent-descriptor dimensions at once (Team A's offensive trend AND Team B's defensive trend), not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For each half separately, compare Team A's goals FOR rate against Team B's goals AGAINST rate within that half. Measure whether the half in which Team B is most defensively vulnerable (second half) aligns or misaligns with the half in which Team A is most productive, and whether the cross-team half-level asymmetry predicts total goals by half.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the attacking team's stronger scoring half misaligns with the defending team's weaker defensive half, total goals in the match are distributed differently across halves than when the two half-level profiles align; specifically, second-half goals are elevated when the defending team's second-half concession rate is high regardless of the attacking team's own half-split
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's second-half goal production relative to first-half goal production differs from Team B's half-split pattern in an asymmetric way. Team A scores more in the first half (0.716) than the second half (0.679), while Team B concedes more in the second half (0.852) than the first half (0.667). This asymmetric within-match half-level split across the two teams — one team's scoring peak misaligning with the opponent's defensive vulnerability peak — is a structurally distinct relationship from either team's half-split read in isolation.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team relationship across two distinct observables (Team A goals FOR by half vs Team B goals AGAINST by half) requiring within-match half-level resolution and a joint two-team conditioning, not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team B's cards_2h FOR rate is above competition baseline AND Team A's cards_2h AGAINST rate is above competition baseline simultaneously. Measure whether total second-half cards in those matches are elevated relative to matches where only one condition holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total second-half cards rise when the away team's own card-proneness and the home team's ability to draw cards from opponents are both simultaneously above competition baseline, with the joint condition producing greater elevation than either alone
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's second-half card rate (cards_2h FOR = 1.605) is notably higher than Team A's second-half card rate (cards_2h FOR = 1.296), while Team A concedes more second-half cards (1.741) than Team B concedes (1.370). The joint cross-team asymmetry in second-half disciplinary behaviour — one team being more card-prone in the second half while the opponent draws more cards from opponents in the second half — creates a compounding second-half card environment that is not captured by either team's cards_2h observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires joint conditioning on two distinct team-role observables (Team B cards_2h FOR and Team A cards_2h AGAINST) simultaneously, with within-match half-level resolution, not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the home team's possession exceeds a threshold above their own long-run baseline AND the away team's corners AGAINST (RECENT_5) is simultaneously elevated above their own ALL_PRIOR baseline. Measure whether corner kicks FOR the home team in those matches are elevated beyond what possession alone or corners-allowed alone would predict.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Corner kicks FOR the dominant-possession team rise with possession share in a non-linear fashion, with the relationship steepening when the opponent's recent corner-allowance rate is also elevated; the joint condition of high possession AND high opponent corner-allowance produces greater corner generation than either condition alone
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession has surged in recent matches (RECENT_5: 59.0%) relative to their long-run average (ALL_PRIOR: 50.7%), while Team B's possession has declined (RECENT_5: 47.4% vs ALL_PRIOR: 50.6%). Simultaneously, Team A's corner kicks FOR have also risen recently (RECENT_5: 5.0 vs ALL_PRIOR: 4.15) while Team B concedes more corners recently (RECENT_5: 7.8 vs ALL_PRIOR: 5.7). The joint relationship between possession dominance and corner kick generation — where a team gaining possession share above a threshold generates disproportionately more corners — is a non-linear interaction between two distinct observables that cannot be reduced to either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint relationship between two distinct observables (possession and corner_kicks) with a potential non-linear/threshold dependence on possession level, conditioned simultaneously on two team-descriptor dimensions (Team A possession trend AND Team B corner-allowance trend). Not reducible to one observable with one band.
